rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says the explicit noun phrase rather than a pronoun generalizes the order to all creatures; “the Merciful” also signals mercy in these proofs for reflective observers.
rows.anchor: ليشعر أن جميع المخلوقات جار على هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command asks people to renew their reflection on creation until observation confirms the truth and removes doubt.
rows.anchor: أي عادوا الاعتبار وتأمل ما تشاهده من هذه المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Futūr means cracks or fissures.
rows.anchor: أي من صدوع وشقوق , ثم أمر تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads karratayn as repeated passes: the eye returns subdued and exhausted, unable to find a flaw after repeated inspection.
rows.anchor: فيحسر البصر من طول التكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This scrutiny applies throughout creation and, once prompted, makes the Prophet’s truth manifest; later signs in al-Mulk repeat the proof.
rows.anchor: إذ هذا الاعتبار بما ذكر من عمومه جار في كل المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proofs developed in al-Mulk, which surpass ordinary rational insight, could not issue from someone insane; the accusations of madness, sorcery, poetry, and lying are false.
rows.anchor: فأنى يصدر بعض عن متصف ببعض ما هزئوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s concise, miraculous order and harmony are beyond human minds; the challenge says humans and jinn cannot produce its like.
rows.anchor: قد انقطعت دونها أنظار العقلاء فكيف ببسطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse answers the opponents’ closing claim that Muhammad is mad, recorded at the end of the sūra.
rows.anchor: جوابا لقوله تعالى في آخر السورة إنه لمجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says denial precedes the quoted accusation to honor the Prophet and soften its impact; placing praise of his character before the accusation heightens that honor.
rows.anchor: وتقدم الجواب بنفي قولهم والتنزيه عنه على حكاية قولهم ليكون أبلغ في إجلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s freedom from contradiction is another proof supporting the Prophet’s truth and this denial.
rows.anchor: ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because an insane person has neither ordered action nor coherent speech, the promised reward implicitly proves the Prophet’s reason more powerfully than an explicit assertion would.
rows.anchor: أثبت له الأجر المستلزم للعقل فيتحقق إثباته من أحكم الحكماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward consoles Muhammad for bearing the burdens of prophethood and enduring the opponents’ abuse.
rows.anchor: على ما تحملت من أثقال النبوة وعلى صبرك عليهم بما يرمونك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward is neither cut off nor diminished in this life or the next, and no person can reproach the Prophet as though he owed it as a favor.
rows.anchor: أي مقطوع ولا منقوص في دنياك ولا في آخرتك ولا لأحد من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward follows righteous work, which flows from character; righteous work therefore results from good character and sound reason.
rows.anchor: فصالحه نتيجة الأخلاق الحسنة والعقل الراجح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a rewarded person might have only modest reason, Muhammad stands at its highest rank; the opponents’ lack of happiness follows their lack of reason.
rows.anchor: بين أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم في أعلاها بقوله مؤكدا لما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great character is Islam, the Qur’anic way Muhammad called people to: neither hardship bends him from it nor gifts turn him aside.
rows.anchor: وهو الإسلام الذي دعا إليه القرآن

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha testified that the Prophet’s character was the Qur’an and that he moved or rested only according to its commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: بشهادة أعرف الناس به زوجه أم المؤمنين الصديقة عائشة بنت الصديق أبي بكر

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says God displayed power in Jesus, efficacy in Āṣif, wrath in Moses’ staff, and divine qualities and noble character in Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي : أظهر الله قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq denotes outward form, while khuluq is inward form and is used for good character.
rows.anchor: أن الخلق والخلق صورتان : الخلق صور الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good character toward God is reverence; toward His rulings it is patience, gratitude, and willing obedience; toward people it is fairness and gracious companionship.
rows.anchor: فمع الله بالتعظيم والإجلال ومع حكمه بالصبر في الضراء والبأساء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that character contains religion, from which submission, humility, self-sacrifice for God, and bearing hardship arise.
rows.anchor: روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says Islam, the noblest religion, was given modesty as its finest character, and modesty gives life to the heart.
rows.anchor: أعطاه الله تعالى أقوى الأخلاق وأشرفها وهو الحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says every religion has a defining character and Islam’s is modesty; modesty is the life of the heart.
rows.anchor: أن لكل دين خلقا وخلق الإسلام الحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet embodied pardon, recognized good, and turning away from the ignorant; he forgave and kindly served even the man who pulled his cloak.
rows.anchor: فكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يأخذ العفو ويأمر بالعرف ويعرض عن الجاهلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī maps nūn to governing speech, the pen to universal effective decree, and writing to detailed, irrevocable destiny unfolding according to decree.
rows.anchor: فقد اشتمل الكلام التدبيري المشار إليه بالنون والقضاء الكلي التأثيري المشار إليه بالقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A waterwheel illustrates the sequence: an engineer plans its parts, builders execute the plan, then the ox, wheel, and channels operate according to it.
rows.anchor: ومثال ذلك أن من أراد بناء دولاب احتاج أولا إلى مهندس يدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decreed outcome divides into wretched and blessed; judgment is hidden and remains one of God’s secrets.
rows.anchor: فالحكم باطن وهو سر من أسراره سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise means Muhammad’s slanderers will soon know the truth as certainly as though they saw it.
rows.anchor: علم الذين رموك بالبهتان علما هو كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two groups are Muhammad and his companions versus their enemies; the question asks which is afflicted by deviation or madness, or where madness has taken hold.
rows.anchor: ولما كان صلى الله عليه وسلم هو ومن معه فريقا

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says al-maftūn can be a verbal noun meaning madness in Quraysh usage, like maʿqūl for reason and majlūd for fortitude.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : مصدر مثل المفتون وهو الجنون بلغة قريش

words: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows who strays and who is guided because He created them; the verse grounds the judgment in certain, comprehensive knowledge.
rows.anchor: إن ربك أي الذي رباك أحسن تربية وجبلك على أعظم الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī cites the saying that the secret of predestination will only become manifest on the Day of al-Ḥāqqah.
rows.anchor: وهذا سر القدر الذي يقال : إنه إنما يظهر يوم الحاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addresses Muhammad but intends his community, urging steadfastness when persecution might tempt even a sensible person to compromise.
rows.anchor: وهو خطاب له صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد أمته ليكون ذلك أبلغ في سماعهم

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malwī says denial corrupts the intellectual and speaking faculties and is the root of every unbelief, deviation, innovation, and evil.
rows.anchor: قال الملوي : ولا يخفى أن كل كفر ظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tudhin means to soften and accommodate some of their demands, compromising by ceasing to forbid shirk, criticize their idols, or condemn their ancestors.
rows.anchor: أي تلاين فتوافق على بعض ما يريدون فتهادنهم على ترك نهيهم عن الشرك

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barrajān defines idhān as accommodating falsehood and knowingly overlooking the truth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : والأدهان ملاينة وانجرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word idhān derives from oil because oil softens what is anointed.
rows.anchor: وهو من الدهن لأنه يلين ما يدهن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fayudhinūn is coordinated with waddū, not the answer to law; their softness is deceptive, and they delayed it to make Muhammad initiate the compromise.
rows.anchor: لا جواب ( لو ) لأجل تنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a reported occasion for al-Kāfirūn, the opponents proposed that Muhammad worship their gods for a year while they worshipped his God for a year.
rows.anchor: كما قيل في سبب نزول ( الكافرون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet prostrated while reciting al-Najm, disbelievers, believers, jinn, and humans followed; some emigrants in Abyssinia returned believing Quraysh had converted, then found otherwise.
rows.anchor: حتى أنهم سجدوا وراءه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما تلا عليهم سورة النجم فسجد فيها

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī compares their wish for Muhammad to compromise with a sick person wishing everyone else sick.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : من أصبح عليلا تمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥallāf is someone who habitually dares to swear excessively, even when his denial is not openly apparent.
rows.anchor: أي مبالغ في الاجتراء على الأيمان وإن لم يظهر لك تكذيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means a general prohibition applying to every oath-swearer, rather than a prohibition on a generic class as a whole.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد النهي عن العموم بل عموم النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rejecting rational and transmitted proofs, Biqāʿī rejects any binding covenant with God that would require Him to grant the deniers what they choose.
rows.anchor: وكان قد بقي أن الإنسان ربما عاهد غيره على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balighah may mean an oath reaching the utmost force of confirmation, or an oath whose term endures until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي أن بلوغها هو البلوغ لا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim would grant the deniers alone, rather than Muslims, whatever good they decree for themselves with a ruler’s binding authority.
rows.anchor: أي تفعلونه فعل الحاكم الذي يلزم قوله لعلو أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the question seeks knowledge, Biqāʿī explains that sal is linked to its second object, though its expected preposition would be ʿan.
rows.anchor: على مطلوبها الثاني وكان حقه أن يعدى بعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zaʿīm can mean guarantor, surety, chief, leader, or a speaker making a true or false claim.
rows.anchor: أي كفيل وضامن أو سيد أو رئيس أو متكلم بحق أو باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunting challenge exposes them: despite hostility and rivalry, none dares guarantee their claim because the Qur’an is true and their arguments false.
rows.anchor: فلم يجسر لما تعلمون من حقية هذا القرآن وما لأقوالهم كلها من العراقة في البطلان أحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After denying rational proof, transmitted proof, and a firm covenant for equating the deniers with Muslims, the argument turns to any alleged partners beyond God.
rows.anchor: ولما نفى أن يكون لهم منه سبحانه في تسويتهم بالمسلمين دليل عقلي أو نقلي أو عهد وثيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation “a great light before which they fall prostrate” does not conflict with the readings of severity or unveiling.
rows.anchor: عن نور عظيم يخرون له سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unveiling serves worship: prostration marks outward submission and signals the inward devotion it contains.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا الكشف الذي كشف لهم المعاني في هذا القرآن إنما هو لأجل العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day the summons to prostrate rebukes and humiliates them for refusing it in earthly life; it is not a new act of worship or legal obligation.
rows.anchor: توبيخا على تركه الآن وتنديما وتعنيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive construction signals their desire to submit and willingness to answer any caller.
rows.anchor: بانيا للمفعول دلالة على إرادتهم للانقياد ورغبتهم فيه من أي داع كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says legal responsibility ends only when each of the two groups enters its own abode.
rows.anchor: وهو دال على أن التكليف لا ينقطع إلا بدخول كل من الفريقين داره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their backs and limbs become one unbending plane, so each attempt to prostrate turns them onto their backs.
rows.anchor: فكلما أرادوا أن يسجدوا انقلبوا على أقفائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says this matches an authentic hadith describing a heart-sick person whose back becomes one vertebra and who falls back whenever he tries to prostrate.
rows.anchor: مطابقة لما ورد في الحديث الصحيح على أن من كان في قلبه مرض في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are raised in the state in which they died and gathered in the state in which they were raised, good for good and evil for evil.
rows.anchor: يبعث المرء على ما مات عليه ويحشر على ما بعث عليه إن خيرا فخيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāshiʿah means humble and submissive; the eyes disclose what is in the heart.
rows.anchor: لأن ما في القلب يعرف في العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers will raise faces brighter than the sun, while the faces of disbelievers and hypocrites will be black and dark.
rows.anchor: أن المؤمنين يرفعون رؤوسهم ووجوههم أضوأ من الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarhaquhum means shame covers and overpowers them, a great humiliation caused by using God-given limbs for pleasures that distance them from Him.
rows.anchor: لأنهم استعملوا الأعضاء التي أعطاهموها سبحانه وتعالى ليتقربوا بها إليه

words: وَقَدْ كَانُوا۟ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَٰلِمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had been called to prostrate in earthly life by callers to God but refused, though physically able; arrogance, not bodily weakness, held them back.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا من كل داع يدعو إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sālimūn means physically sound and able, with no bodily impediment to prostration.
rows.anchor: وإنما يمنعهم منه الشماخة والكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses iḥtibāk: inability in the first verse implies omitted ability in the second, while safety in the second implies omitted unsafety in the first.
rows.anchor: ذكر عدم الاستطاعة أولا دال على حذف الاستطاعة ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī links the judgment to earlier denials of resurrection and of following one human, citing the objections in al-Qamar and al-Muʾminūn.
rows.anchor: فإن الامر فيهم دائر بين عاد وثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd is named first because its land is nearer Quraysh, making its destruction a stronger warning; its cry resembles the Trumpet’s blast that scatters the dead.
rows.anchor: أن بلادهم أقرب إلى قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added description al-qāriʿah intensifies awe: it strikes the ears and world as heaven splits, stars scatter, and mountains are uprooted.
rows.anchor: أي تضرب ضربا قويا وتدق دقا عنيفا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account first groups both peoples in denial, then distinguishes their punishments because of that denial.
rows.anchor: ولما جمعهم في التكذيب , فصلهم في التعذيب لأجل ذلك التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd are the people of the prophet Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: وهم قوم صالح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording focuses on the tangible horror of the punishment, rather than on the source from which it came.
rows.anchor: بنى للمجهول قوله : { فأهلكوا } أي بأيسر أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭāghiyah is a cry exceeding all bounds of severity, making the earth and hearts tremble.
rows.anchor: أي الصيحة التي جاوزت الحد في الشدة فرجفت منها الأرض والقلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd are the people of the prophet Hūd.
rows.anchor: وهم قوم هود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣarṣar wind combined extreme cold and piercing sound, intensified until the cold burned and the sound deafened.
rows.anchor: أي هي في غاية ما يكون من شدة البرد والصوت كأنه كرر فيها البرد حتى صار يحرق بشدته

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malwī says the root ṣarr denotes severe cold or severe heat.
rows.anchor: وقال الملوي : أصله صر وهو البرد الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀtiyah means beyond bounds in force and destructive gusts; its custodians could not restrain it, and it tore people from shelters and fortified homes.
rows.anchor: أي مجاوز للحد من شدة عصفها وعظمة قصفها

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Ibn ʿAbbās report that winds and rain normally descend measured by an angel, except the Flood and ʿĀd’s wind, which God let overwhelm their keepers.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind’s unprecedented force shows that God created and directed it by choice, not nature, as punishment for those who denied His rule and the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: كانت بقدرته واختياره قهرا لمن طعن في ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakhkharahā means He compelled and controlled the wind over them; the wording marks punitive subjection rather than mercy or discipline.
rows.anchor: والتسخير : استعمال الشيء بالاقتدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nights are listed first because calamities are more dreadful in darkness, with fewer helpers and hidden sources; the seven also signal fullness and emphasis.
rows.anchor: وقدم الليالي لأن المصايب فيها أفظع وأقبح وأشنع لقلة المغيث والجهل بالمأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥusūmā is the plural of ḥāsim: relentless, continuous, and destructive, like repeated cauterization; the wind struck without pause and eradicated them.
rows.anchor: جمع حاسم أي بحس مانع من التصرف دائم متتابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The days were called the Days of the Old Woman, either after the old woman the wind dragged from hiding or because they fell at winter’s end; Biqāʿī gives the interval from Wednesday to the next Wednesday in Shawwāl.
rows.anchor: أو لأنها عجز الشتاء وهي ذات برد ورياح شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight days and seven nights show the storm began by day; had it begun at night, the day and night counts would not differ this way.
rows.anchor: وقد لزم من زيادة عدد الأيام أن الابتداء كان بها قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lay dead, crushed, and humiliated; ṣarʿā is the plural of ṣarīʿ, describing the people felled during the full span of the storm.
rows.anchor: أي مجدلين على الأرض موتى معصورين مجهزة على كل منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bodies resemble the trunks of old, hollow date palms, conveying their great size, dismemberment, severed heads, and darkened appearance.
rows.anchor: قد شاخت وهرمت فهي في غاية العجز والهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāwiyah means eaten away inside and fallen, by analogy with a setting star or a house emptied of its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: ومن خوي المنزل - إذا خلا من قطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that the wind entered their mouths and expelled their innards through the rear explains the image of large bodies torn apart and stripped of life.
rows.anchor: كانت تدخل من أفواههم فتخرج ما في أجوافهم من الحشو من أدبارهم
